author: Kaisle
text: Mostly good, and far better than the popular alternatives. Two annoying problems. The Diary doesn't show the items in the accurate order anymore, which makes it hard to check if I entered them correctly. Also, if I open the app and search a food, about half the time, before I finish logging it, the app randomly takes me back to the main screen (with "Today" at the top) and I have to start again, which is frustrating and adds friction to the action that should be the easiest.

author: Jackie Wirtjes
text: For over a year I have not been able to save recipes I create. After entering all of my items, with a combination of scanning, searching the database or adding a new item...every single time the app gives an error. This is not a cheap app and this feature should work. A quick google or reddit search shows tons of people have this problem. Updated rating as recipes now work finally.

author: Julie Sosinski
text: ok I had started to use this app because it was recommended by health coach at work. A trainer at the gym i started going to recommended a different app. So for a bit I was using both to compare the 2 other app more user friendly, but I started a new program and they recommended this app. So i reinstalled it. I don't like having to pay to get the barcode reader, and I found that some of the macros don't calculate correctly when building a recipe. This is important when one is tracking them!

author: DeAnne Falise
text: Update: that's a stupid to add to the notes This sucks that you can't track magnesium for your electrolytes. They don't even have the option to add magnesium when you create a food. Their help site says to create a food and add your supplements there. Hello!!! It's not listed. I mean how hard is it to add it to the list of nutrients. That post was a few years ago and it's still not an option. They have no problem changing the app for the worse. I have premium. I expect to be able to custom add.

author: Isaac Surh
text: Terrible, terrible design. User interface is the most confusing, non-intuitive design imaginable. Also, wildly inconsistent calorie counts for food items. I typed in 1 cup cooked quinoa and saw search results ranging from 120 calories to 225. The search results appeared crowd sourced, so accuracy is dubious. People just write in their opinions, defeats the purpose of counting calories. Stay away from this app.

author: Hard Life
text: I had high hopes for this app, but sadly it is extremely limited. The food database is good, but the tracking is very clunky. The workouts are limited and have a fee for basic functionality. Actually, everything useful is locked behind a paywall and isn't done in a way that makes it appear worth the cost. The bones are there, but this just us not it.

author: Rhonda Allen
text: UPDATE: I had to take this down to 3 stars now because as of how this app has become BOMBARDED with ads AND you can no longer scan barcodes without paying for the premium version of the app which also, by the way, removes the ads. How convenient! Otherwise it's a good app for tracking your food entries and viewing your nutritional intake. Those ads are very annoying though. If the cost wasn't so high I would consider purchasing just to remove them.

author: Courtney Bolton
text: While I have been using the app since 2013, the latest update has ruined the functionality of the app. Previously, I could type a brand name into the search and pull up recent items. Now I have to type in a keyword from the item description. Bring back the ability to search by brand! It also deleted all my recent foods and I now have to re-enter them. An update should make the app better, not break previous functionality!

author: Nicholas & Francesca
text: App is running worse & worse, day by day. This app used to be the best. I recently installed MFP because I started a serious weight loss goal. At first it was working perfectly. I'm familiar with MFP because I had used it 5 years ago to lose weight & it 100% helped me reach my goal then. Now, the app is VERY unreliable. It never picks up my steps from my fitness watch or other apps like Map My Fitness. It's adding exercises on days I've done zero (couch potato days). Very, very unreliable.

author: Sara Vnuk
text: What Am I paying for, if every time I do a search for something I ate within the last day doesn't show up? This is annoying and time consuming. There really isn't much of an advantage to paying for a premium membership if I have to go through all the extra work to find the foods that I'm commonly eating anyway. Perhaps it's an algorithm change to get people to pay for the premium plus. Regardless, I likely will not be renewing my membership.

author: Nick
text: This used to be a great app, but the most recent update is a major step back. Meals you save and then use on another day used to put the exact foods, so you could easily customize amounts. Now the meal gets added as a single item Search algorithm got a huge downgrade. You used to be able to search by maker and no longer can. Searching Starbucks in my recents doesn't bring up my Starbucks drinks, I now need to type the specific drink

author: Don Bergquist
text: Would be Great if it Worked! Unfortunately, even in the Premium+ Subscription at its absolutely PREMIUM (EXPENSIVE!) price, does not work. The app consistently fails to save custom meal targets, defaulting to an even distribution. Website changes for these targets also do not transfer to the app. It does not retain links to third-party apps like Samsung Fitness, requiring daily re-linking for activity tracking. The app's calorie target remains inaccurately high compared to the web calculations.

author: The Sunshine Breakthrough
text: I used to love this app. but nothing works on it. I have paid for premium for years. I still get ads. Now buttons aren't working and I can't log in even though I've updated my phone multiple times. Customer service is probably some bot cause there's no way an IT person is that dumb. I wrote a detailed issue email and it wrote back to try literally all the things I already said I tried. why bother. I'm about to just find a new app I'm so mad.

author: Gregory Bott
text: The lack of even email support is very frustrating. I pay for this app. It has a cool feature that shows macros right on my Android home screen. I can't see the Macros because MyFitnessPal says I have to pay for the app even though I've already paid. Bugs happen. No problem. Poor/non-existent support is unacceptable for a paid product.

author: Bree Sisson
text: This used to be more convenient. A lot of the great features that once were free and made using this app worth it is no longer free. I used to really like using this app to track but now its just extra time consuming and not very many features without paying $20 a month. Not worth it either way in my opinion. I used to use this all the time but has become a hassle without being able to scan the barcode to add it to my log.

author: Michael Cisneros
text: I've been using the app for around a week, the interface is pretty easy to figure out and the data it has already on different foods is actually really good. If you can't find a food you are looking for you can enter the data for it, such as calories, protein, fats, vitamins, etc and save it. One downside I have found with this app is the food scanning is locked behind a paywall. As someone who eats a lot of "custom recipes" that really aren't official, it takes time to create custom recipes.

author: Deaven Swainey
text: It's still the best database and tracker available for free, in my opinion. However, the last version was much better and way, WAY less buggy. One glitch There's a common error that pops up when looking up foods that says something like "You're not online," and you have to go back a screen or force close the app to fix it. Food items or recipes get duplicated 3 times in the food diary, too. Mine still tracks my steps somehow even though I turned off all tracking and connections to health apps.

author: Amanda Littrell
text: I remember when you used to be able to use the barcode scanner for free... I miss that! Made logging more convenient. Not everyone can afford subscriptions to extra apps... would totally give it 5 stars if it still had that in the free version. Other than that, I love it! It's very helpful keeping me in check. Staying on top of my macros and physical activity.

author: Bonnie Block
text: I used this app several years ago, and decided to use it again. It's been working fine for about 10 days, but not any more. It has stopped responding on both my Samsung phone and Samsung tablet. I installed and re-installed and have restarted both devices. I don't know what to do. 2 days later after reinstalling the app, the app is still freezing when I try to add info, and the ability to add daily weight is gone. The app only allows editing weight goal. This app is not functional for me.

author: Anke Farrar
text: Last time I used this app was at least 5years ago and since then, lots of things have changed. Big change, I am absolutely unhappy about is the fact that you can't even use the barcode scanner anymore without having to subscribe to a plan. I get that everyone has to make money and I see the "necessity" to charge for the meal planner, but the bar code scanner, really? I haven't used all featured yet since I just downloaded it yesterday, so I'll see how much more restricted this app is now.

author: Jeff McQuigg
text: Very buggy, inaccurate, easy to make mistakes. I've found 3 large bugs in just a few months using it - simple easy things. As in it can't add macros correctly to compute calories accurately. You think they would have figured that one out on the 1.0 release. How many ppl has this messed up? Practically no QA went into this app. You have to check your entries at the end of the night 2 or 3 times to make sure it got it right.

author: Mark Orme
text: This used to be a great app, clear, easy to use. This is the 2nd time they've "updated" it - to intentionally make it worse. Looks like they'll keep downgrading it until you leave OR buy premium. After using it for years (AND creating their food/nutrition database- bar code scanning is no longer free and easy. NOW, a new layout taking WAY more time to enter information AND NOT intuitive. Time it takes to log calories/nutrition = #1 reason dieters hate logging. They just made it harder

author: Kent Packard
text: Classic example of software that gets worse with new UI updates. Some of the functionality that I thought I was paying for when I purchased my subscription has disappeared, such as customizing the dashboard with what I want to track. The annoying streak celebration popups can't be disabled, and they pop up Every. Single. Day. when I'm trying to enter in my food. the app works great but the incompetence of the UI team is ruining this product.

author: nick villiers
text: Overall FP is good app to log your calories and macros. Luckily the sub doesn't paywall most of the features, like meals, food entry limits ect. I'm taking it down to four stars mainly because they don't give you barcode scanning in the free plan. Either way it's good enough so I don't have to vibe code an alternative for myself. Good job.

author: Emigdio Pockels
text: This app used to be so good. Purchased the annual membership and after I purchased the issues started. It can't find food I previously found or logged. I can't find restaurants like before, sometimes it kicks me out telling me, I dont have internet. There is so much junk now it's confusing. after my membership ends, I think I will delete the account.

author: Vernon Chiu
text: The app is adequate for tracking calories and macros. It has a large library of crowd sourced nutrition information but double check to make sure the information is actually correct. I subscribed to the premium version to test the AI functions, but sadly, the AI-powered calorie counting from pictures produced inaccurate information nearly every time. Best use of the app is to help understand portion sizes and calorie content of various foods to reach your health goals.

author: Cheryl Varner
text: I wanted an app to hold me accountable and this one does the trick, I set it for alerts and can add my food intake with voice to text. It lets you add health data and it lets you know from calories burned, where you're at all along the way. Just a week in, and I'm already seeing some weight loss. Thank you, fitness pal

author: r white
text: When the app works, it's amazing. I've used it since 2023. Love to see my progress and track food, especially with the barcode scanner. There's been an issue with trophies since day 1. Recently there have been glitches. I've synced with Samsung Health since 2023 and now it's not supported. As of this weekend, I get errors when trying to upload pictures.

author: Amber Weatherby (Noa)
text: Good features, the meal tracking is exactly what I was looking for. But the step count breaks down at random intervals. A way to manually add the steps in (not as an exercise, but in the steps feature itself) would be very helpful, since it seems that the sync feature has been problematic for years.

author: C A
text: They give you a week to try the meal scanner for free. If you have a job, but you're using this, you likely aren't the one cooking, so this helps track inputs. It works, mostly to get you started, but you have to tweak serving sizes, or on some misidentified foods, change them. I cancelled because I don't have time to log everything, and if you don't, you have a backlog that you won't ever complete. If this was a smartglasses app- where you can just tell it "log it", it might fit my life.

author: Kellie Simpson
text: Used to be able to use bar codes to scan your food for free. Now you have to pay for that. Accuracy is bare minimum at best. Check your stuff, it may not be accurate. You add stuff according to the calories on your package, they keep that and you get nothing back. You are literally doing the work for them and they want to charge you for those additional benefits that you provided. Been using this app for over 8 years and it just keeps getting worse.

author: Mariah Murrell
text: the new update said it was to make it easier to see everything, but now what you ate is hidden behind each meal and you have to click on each. When you try to do that it adds more food to it instead of letting you see the meal, and then let's you in to delete the ones it just added. You have to manually click on each date, it doesn't let you swipe anymore. It might be okay on a tablet, but it wasn't made for phone usage.

author: Steffanie Brady
text: *Update: STILL can't consistently track Samsung Health steps.* Doesn't cover all vitamins and minerals, so it's utterly useless for tracking them! *Update* STILL can't truly customize nutrition goals. The macro settings are INCREDIBLY limiting, making it very non-functional for personal health and fitness journeys. Overall, it's been a disappointing experience trying this app AGAIN. Sucks to pay for features that don't function. Thankfully, I can finally (usually) save recipes and meals again.

author: Ben B
text: Has gotten worst over time with some major bugs. Two to note, looses access to its food database even when conntected to the internet frequently. Also, logs you out randomly without any reason even if you were logged in recording things in your log. Ive noticed this app slowly slipping into a mess and might be better to look elsewhere for a new basic logging app.

author: Collin Armstrong
text: I use MyFitnessPal every day. Please restore the ability to select and delete multiple food entries at once, as well as a "Delete Meal" option for Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, and Snacks. Deleting items one at a time is slow and frustrating, especially when correcting or rebuilding meals. These features made food logging much more efficient.

author: Gabby Leisure
text: I've been using my fitnesspal for 14 years. This is the first time I'm considering going to a new calorie tracker. The new interface is terrible. You have to click into your meals to see what you've had, it's not as easy to add/modify/review things. The entire thing is just clunky and makes a tedious thing ( calorie tracking) more tedious. I switched the location to Turkey a month or so ago to get the old interface back, but now that one has changed too. Going to the LoseIt App now which is sad.

author: Matt Styka
text: It's really a shame when apps go down a different path almost certainly just out of monetary or data tracking gain. I consistently used the app for a year to great success and now I open the app and I'm being asked to log in. Even as a free user? If you need a login to get premium features, that makes sense. But to now require a login is not something that should be required (and it wasn't for years). I don't like writing negative reviews but sometimes it is necessary. Do better!

author: Katherine Collaco
text: Free version of the app works well enough for tracking macros, plenty of logged foods to select from, and it's easy enough to add your own foods and recipes. There's an occasional glitch where it will log my breakfast twice, so I have to check at the end of the day or next day to make sure everything is correct and delete duplicate entries as needed.

author: Mark Lorance
text: The app used to work perfectly fine until the latest UI overhaul. Super laggy, extra clicks to get where you want, you add a food entry and it's gone when you go back to check it, it doesn't put the items in the order you entered them in, so it's harder to keep track of what you've entered. They're just lucky it's the one app that works with my insurance to save money, otherwise I'd be gone after the latest UI update. Had to write this after the app pooped the bed adding a couple food entries.

author: Dana
text: This app has completely went downhill in the last few months. One MAJOR thing that's been happening for me is when I log my pre-saved meals, some of the individual ingredients will change to 0 cals. So I've been overeating by a lot every day before I realized it started doing this, thanks to the last update. The main purpose of the app is to log calories and it can't even do that correctly. It used to be perfect, but it's been ruined. Save your time and do not bother.

author: sarah clark
text: I pay for the premium version and it used to be great. off&on I have used MyFitnessPal for over a decade & I've always been happy with it. I hadn't used it in about a year so I signed back on since I'm still paying for it, and this new interface is HORRIBLE. it's not intuitive at all! I keep accidentally logging previous meals which takes several clicks to undo and the (not) quick add calorie only function is now hidden behind several clicks. I may cancel but I'm hopeful they will improve MFP :)

author: Kendall Embry
text: Continues to regress. What was once a powerhouse for tracking calories has turned into a paywall nightmare. Lost the barcode scanning years ago to a paid subscription, so adjusted by typing more clearly. Now, the ability to choose restaurants and simply add the ingredients (like Chipotle or Subway) are gone. After using this app for many years I am finally done with it. Do not waste your time or money.

author: Melissa Van Hoose
text: The new UI makes everything harder to see quickly and more steps to do. I can no longer easily see my entire day's food diary because I have to click on each meal individually to see what is in it. There is too much crammed together on the page and every field has too much padding, so you always have to scroll to get down to your diary. It worked well before and was compact. I have been using this app for 14 years and now looking for an alternative.

author: Brittany Tingle
text: This app has not kept up with technology. I was excited to get back on my fitness journey after 10 years. I used this app before and loved it, but its exactly the same as it used to be, but more expensive. Still tons of barcodes that don't work (why do I have to hand-enter them when we have AI?), trying to import recipes is an absolute joke. I've basically paid to hand-enter every single meal even though I use HelloFresh, the most common meal prep. don't even try to take a photo and log it.

author: Kellee Huffaker
text: Somehow this app makes my life harder when shouldn't it be the opposite? I think the recipe adding feature has only worked once for me. Every other time I get an error or find 7 or so exact same recipes on my list the next day from all the attempts to add. I need this feature to work, I don't have time for it to take an entire minute and a half to load just to tell me an error occurred. My personal trainer requires that I use this app though so I'll have to stick it out. Please fix it!!

author: matthew jdj
text: It is an okay app. The problem I have with it is that free users have to search for every food that they had. And when you do look it up they have a bunch of different options of the same food but different calories. super confusing. Not only that but the scanning feature and the barcode feature are all locked behind a paywall. witch is $20 A MONTH which is crazy. And the app is also super buggy.

author: Merissa Lucas
text: it's just ok. I'm not going to pay for this, the price is insane. I only use it to count calories and protein. What is annoying about this app? Most prepackaged foods are not available on here or hard to find when I search them - Or, f they are available they will have several listed and they all have different calories and macros for the exact same product or item. Random people must be putting them in wrong.

author: Lana Richie
text: glitches sometimes and has to be Uninstalled and redownloaded. does the job. there are better options now but I've used this one for so long that it is just easier to stick with. some of the paid features are free on other apps. mainly the scanning option but it doesn't take long to type in what you are looking for. I've lost weight using this twice, once before pregnancy and once after in my early 40's. tracking macros works, no matter how you choose to do it

author: Alisa H
text: This app is great when it works. The new feature to copy a meal from one day to the next is fantastic. However, it just doesn't work half the time I want to use it. I can't even tell you all the problems I have getting into the app and logging food because the character limit here prevents me. I truly want to love this app and recommend it fully, but I just can't. It's so buggy and frustrating. Not to mention features that were free several years ago cost money (booo!).

author: Stoutzombie
text: Ad depented calorie counter. I have used this app off and on over 14 years. In the beginning, you could scan the barcode of an item and add it. It would tell you your daily intake of fats and sugars and vitamins. Now, you need an auxiliary app to scan barcodes, and it only shows carbs, fats, and proteins unless you navigate to one of its sub menus, using one of the clunkiest interfaces I have seen. All while pushing premium subscription and alternative apps to " Enhance" your experience it.

author: Phillup Ciadella
text: I've used this app for years and used to love it, but over the past couple of years it has become frustrating to use. Features that I used to rely for quick and easy logging, like remembering recent exercises and foods, no longer works. Additionally the app will randomly log me out while I'm in the middle of trying to log something. MyFitnessPal used to be the perfect easy to use app, but has been updated into being a buggy and unintuitive mess.

author: Wayne Baptiste
text: Update: Now the app logs me out randomly. Getting closer to unusable. Just don't sign up for their premium, because even if you recieve a refund on what should've been a cancelled subscription (before the renew date), you'll still get a retry charge 2 weeks later. Support will also say "sorry, can't help you". The app used to be less buggy, but food entries water logs get deleted randomly. Inconsistent tracking on 4 out of 7 days. So stay on top of it, and I guess you'll be fine.

author: Donnie Francis
text: Been using this app for years prior to the addition of "premium" & "premium plus" The constant ads & prompts to pay is annoying. The price too high. Was aggravating when I opened the app to find out I was no longer able to do certain things I was able to do prior when the "premium" addition was added. Doesn't allow me to even search for anything. This app had become nothing but a trash money grab. The greed is real

author: J_Owens
text: I haven't used MyFitnessPal in a couple of years, but wanted to try it again. Unfortunately, it lasted less than 24 hours on my phone. Not being able to use the barcode scanner unless you're paying the premium service is a deal-breaker and quite ridiculous. The barcode scanner has been part of MyFitnessPal forever. There must be plenty of people out there willing to pay for that feature but I am not one of them.

author: Shannon McLain
text: I've enjoyed the app but just noticed that when I add exercise it increases my calories, I wish I could remove that but still log exercise. I also think that the barcode scanner should be part of the free option, I can see macros settings and nuanced things being charged for but the scanner would really help newbies and encourage us... I might be looking for something else but so far the catalog has had all my items.

author: Leonard G
text: I used to think this was an amazing app but now it's just ok. Putting one of the best features (the barcode scanner) behind a paywall is absolute BS! Loyal fans now have to pay $20 a month just to be able to scan food barcodes in order to post it to our Diary. These people used to care about making it as easy as possible for people to keep up on our Diaries, now it seems like they only care about $$$. I'll keep using it until I find an app that's better... one that isn't greedy.

author: William Hinkle
text: You've made updates to the UI which weren't really needed. You should, instead, focus on the search functionality. Improvements in substring searches would be great. Please add a session timeout check to it too, because when your session dies, the search just stops functioning and the app doesn't kick you back to login. Speaking of login, biometrics would be a nice add. Also, there are a while lot of "verified" foods which are simply incorrect. Please clean up your database.

author: Luis Sendejas
text: ive been using this app for years to track my calories and absolutely loved it up until now the new ui is absolutely horrendous and inefficient. theres no reason why I should have to click through multiple windows just to edit, add, remove, or even just to look at all the food ive eaten for the day. please change it back or ill be forced to switch to a different app.

author: Kaeli
text: I found a lot of value in this app prior to the most recent update, but the app is much less intuitive/user friendly than it used to be. Features meant to be helpful are frustrating, and I waste time correcting and deleting mistakes, which was never an issue before. Will be looking for an alternative Update: changing from two stars to one because no matter what food I search it says the food doesn't exist and I can only create my own foods lol, this is a new issue I haven't had before

author: Kelsea Reagan
text: I liked the old version not the new updated version. it's hard to see everything because everything is separate where before it was together. for example: your food and exercise would show separate but in the same column. so you could tell how many calories you have eaten before the amount of calories you've burned would be calculated.

author: Sarah Kale
text: I used to love this app. I've been using it off & on for over a decade. Now that the newsfeed is gone, it's no better than any other calorie tracking app. This change is an epic fail. 2026.. it's gotten worse!! now it's so much more complicated to input food. I'm going to start trying to log directly through my FitBit app instead. shame Ive been using this for over a decade & now It's awful.

author: Sandra Morris
text: Great way to monitor what you eat daily, weekly etc. The free version is adequate for the basic calories, nutrients, goals; the premium has a lot more in depth features - pretty cool. The extra bells and whistles are beyond my budget right now. That's OK cuz the basic, free version is perfect for me. I have a hard time sticking with my best intentions and this is proving to be a good way to set up healthy habits and create an ongoing plan to meet consistent nutrition goals.

author: Liberty Penna
text: i like this app, the free version gives me everything i need. my one wish, is that for quick add entries, i wish i could name the entry or leave a note. sometimes quick add when i know the calorie amount is more efficient than searching for existing foods that aren't in the app or the nutrition info is wrong. i'd want to write down what it was i ate in the quick add entry.

author: Aaron Dodson
text: Edit: app is becoming unusable. Can't search for anything. Type in Chicken vindaloo, no results. Type in garlic naan, no results. Type in whole milk, no results. Been using this app for almost ten years and I'm thinking it's about time to wrap it up. Was great till they got greedy and made scanning barcodes a premium feature. $80 a year for premium? Absolutely not lol they are out of their minds.

author: Alicia Krol
text: I've been using MFP for over a decade now. The latest UI is awful. 1). accidentally clicking the log yesterdays meal is too easy, and then having to manually click each item to delete it is time consuming. 2) the popup that takes up the whole screen saying yay X number of days streak, every day, is patronizing and feels like they are talking to a toddler. and it keeps me from making the change I need to make. at least have an option to turn it off. I already submitted an MFP ticket.

author: Abigail Fisk
text: App sucks now. It's gotten more and more bloated over the years, I hate the annoying streak pop-ups every single day you log. Also the app has a bunch of weird, annoying bugs, like the weight graph starting on the current day and just showing a straight line into the future. Very often when I relog a meal from the previous day, it will add twice. It kind of feels like the app is vibe-coded which sucks.

author: Sharon Friar
text: I'm not a fan of this new version in general, after using my fitness pal premium version for years. Things are counterintuitive to locate, And I find myself using other apps that are just frankly easier. I also hate on the micro tracking that the columns are now average /goal/left... I only want to see goal/left... That average column is just added noise on an already crowded page

author: Renee
text: 10+ years using this app and ive always loved it until the most recent update. It is not user friendly at all. Requires more clicks for basic things. I am most frustrated but it glitching and being unable to tell me the accurate number of macros ive logged for the day. One spot says 174 carbs, then other 220 carbs.... it doesn't make any sense and hate that I pay for a premium subscription. I've given the update 2 months and it is still awful. I want my money back.

author: Benjamin Shaibu
text: For all its flaws, I still use it for tracking calories and macronutrients. It has a large bank updated by users - so be careful with confirming foods. It has some good charts. Integrations are unreliable (e.g. Strava import). Menus are hidden behind multiple clicks e.g. finding the weight progress menu can be a chore. The app keeps adding "improvements" that make it harder to use e.g. clicking through multiple screens to get to the place to log a meal or water.

author: A Rojas
text: This app has slowly chipped away at all of the features that made it good and and put them behind a paywall. I rated it 5 stars in 2013. I am happy after switching to Samsung Health, which never disconnects from my watch, tries to sell me anything extra, and doesn't even force ads on me. They're already using my data for who knows what, might as well let me use the data that users like me helped to build. The only reason I'm giving it 2 stars instead of 1 is because the calorie database is huge.

author: Brandon S. Frazer
text: Overall a better app than Cronometer and less bugs as well. I would prefer MFP tracked micros and didn't require a food to be logged (Like Cronometer) as breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack. The latter is really a waste of time and forced rigidity. There should be an opt out of this anachronistic way of eating.

author: Brian Gapp
text: Errors with calories burned in past days. It increases to a greater number of calories burned each day when looking at it in reverse. Not accurate. This is some error which occurs while syncing to Google Fit via Android Health Connect to import steps and calories burned... which seems very base level. I just want to give this 5 stars but the issue is unfortunate so 4 stars for now.

author: Rebecca M
text: was a good app. latest update on the free version is not good. took away useful dashboard view, changed buttons so it is too easy to fat-finger the wrong options, harder to see an overview of the foods for a whole day. adds are now intrusive. more clicks to do less. it briefly went back to old version, and i thought they realized how bad the update was. no, appears they think this is better. I keep trying, but its now just too hard to use. not worth it. will be changing to a different app.

author: Nichol
text: The app itself is good. My issue comes with the recipes. I have only been casually glancing at them as I downloaded the app yesterday. Many of the recipes either don't include all the ingredients shown in picture ( no salad greens for a salad?), have insane amounts listed ( for another dish , 5 cups lettuce and 23 cups of cabbage!?)or the directions are vague at best. I have been a home cook for a long time and can figure this out but the poor people new to this are likely to get frustrated.

author: Laura Wright
text: Kind of a load of nonsense that you have to pay for the premium just for the barcode scanning function.... especially when other apps have it for free. I'd prefer to use this as my one stop all things calorie counting (activity, food, etc.) but not about to pay for a different version. 🙄

author: Leinad Znarf
text: No fees. No constant hassle. EXACTLY what I needed. This is a well thought out APP with tons of options and customizability. I've tested at least 10. This app is superior. Love that it includes exercise of all types, water, you name it. If the price was say...$4/month or $35 annually I'd subscribe to Premium. They've got to lower the price. I'd even recommend it on social media.

author: Shawna C
text: I've been using this app to track meals, weight, macros, and exercise since 2017. I like this app for the ease of use. Most foods are already in the app and if not they can be added as well as adding personal recipes. The app connects with my Garmin watch and app to track my activity seamlessly. Down over 100lbs with the help of the app. I only wish the Beta version for tracking GLP1 would track the oral medication not just the injectables. Maybe that will come after the Beta version.

author: Jo L
text: If you don't pay to play, you may as well be tracking your macros and calories yourself. Everything is manual input. This app seems to think I'm going to intuit my calorie burn. Why would I pay if the free version (preview) is this bad? Edit: their latest update makes it impossible to input food. apparently, this app doesn't know what flax seed is or even oatmeal. This app is a joke!

author: Sean Silva
text: Please revert back - the latest changes were not necessary and the interface is difficult to navigate now. I used to be able to quick add calories and now that's hidden inside of the log button. The app also randomly logs me out. This is MyFitnessPal, not a banking app or something - there's no need to log users out so frequently.

author: Salvador Araya
text: update: the new changes have made me leave this app and go to a competitor. thx for the memories. 💔 I hate the new UI changes. everything was fine before wth! everything is so big now and requires more scrolling, more swiping, and more taps/clicks that previously were trivial things like moving a food item from breakfast to lunch. if I could install the old version i would. but the old version wasn't even syncing anymore and I lost a 345 DAY STREAK because of them!! bring back classic UI!

author: Ayame Shimitsu
text: Removed a lot of features over the years or things that used to be free are now charged. still a system I use the most and seemed the most accurate but disappointment how everything seems to be getting worse. If you're too poor for a subscription you have to work harder to guess things and lose weight.

author: Deisy Blanford
text: The biggest frustration with MyFitnessPal is the step syncing. My Samsung Watch 8 syncs perfectly with Samsung Health, but MyFitnessPal consistently shows the wrong step count. I've disconnected and reconnected the accounts multiple times, cleared the cache, and checked permissions, but the syncing is still inaccurate. I chose MyFitnessPal specifically for step syncing, so this has been really disappointing. I actually preferred Calo for food scanning and logging, but switched. to log activity.

author: Chris B.
text: I like it so much I purchased a subscription. The fasting tracker could be improved though. I use a separate app for that. The exercise app would be better if I could label workouts and change the exercises within each workout as needed. But as far as a calorie tracker, macro counter it's good. A plus being the integration with Google Health.

author: Robert
text: Please roll back the UI "enhancement"! You can no longer swipe left and right quickly switch between days. You can no longer see on one page everything logged for the day - instead you have to tap each meal to see everything. UI changes should make things more convenient, not more cumbersome. The only good change is the "Log yesterday's meal again" feature.

author: Elizabeth Shuler
text: The barcode scanner is super convenient. I like that I can customize my macros. The recent update is frustrating. You used to be able to move foods between meals, but now you have to delete each item and then load it on the meal where you want it. I just upgraded to premium+ for meal planning and I'm already disappointed. My first planned meal is a pink salad, which has a lot of fruit in it, but the nutritional facts say 0g sugar. I feel like I can't trust the planner to meet my macros.

author: Kathryn Parker
text: at this point I'm considering uninstalling though I have used it for years. they keep breaking all the features that made it great. it's now difficult to log food in the diary, view it for accuracy, enter new foods or ingredients and switching between days is now annoying and finnicky. It's like they keep adding features to the and encourage people to pay but it's backfiring as they arethings that make the user experience worse, and users less likely to use either the paid or free version.

author: Holly O'Neil
text: I loved the old version of the app -- it was simple, straightforward, and had everything a user needed. The new version is inundated with ads, does not allow you to view your meals as a whole, and miscalculates macros. It seems like the company destroyed the app for the sake of ad space.

author: Tina Specht
text: AWFUL! The updates fix glitches, but not the changes that ruined the app. LIST 1: can't swipe back & forth between days, can't delete more than 1 entry at a time, now requires multiple steps/clicks to get to information. Addition of medication log & feelings is stupid & doesn't add enough to offset damage to app. I pay for premium subscription & just deleted my auto renew. I'm not paying for an app that was reliable & helpful in my health journey that is now practically worthless.

author: Lola Knudsen
text: I am forced to use this to log food in my Withings app. If I would have known this I would have gone with a different scale. This app is insanely priced compared to others. It's full of ads and the calorie counts are wrong. you can't type in Costco or Starbucks to find foods. So I'm going to keep using mynetdiary, and manually put the food into myfitnesspal. Two foods in both apps myfitnesspal has the wrong count.

author: Rana Haddad
text: Quitting the app after 15 years. the recent UI update is unbelievably unintuitive, burdensome, visually confusing, adds several extra steps to complete the same actions, and is just straight up ugly. Making people pay to scan barcodes is one thing. A backwards UI overhaul to hell is another, and I've reached my breaking point.

author: Caitlin Domina
text: Great for tracking, but with the premium plus membership, I would expect to see more recipes in the meal planner module. Plenty or recipes under recipe discovery, with macros and micros, so no reason why those can't be available to select from in the meal planner. Would love to see this enhancement made soon or I will not consider renewing my premium plus access.

author: Ariel Rivera
text: I feel like this app still doesnt incorporate weights or estimated calories burned with it. The most annoying is that the app doesnt sync to your fitbit (google health) even if it says its connected. Ive literally logged in disconnected and reconnected the app, etc. and it STILL doesnt migrate my steps over. its annoying and frustrating and makes me not want to keep this app. Please, fix this. This is a fitness app and its not even properly working. also, stop making everything Premium.

author: Jenn Thomas
text: Not sure if its something I am doing wrong in the app but my meal plans for each day are always taking me over my allowable Fat per day. I double checked all the settings for the percentages/grams are set etc. I didnt update anything midweek either. any help with this would be appreciated! I have been staying on goal according to the app so far which is a great app overall!

author: Mike Denny
text: Going down hill. Used to be able to scan barcodes and then that was made a pay feature. I have been voice typing for years, but now the app and only this app glitches when voice typing. It starts searching when you type or voice type the first word and cuts off the rest. Almost like they are forcing you to pay for barcode. Greedy.

author: Dawn Housden
text: 98% of the time I like this app. I like the fact it works with google/fitbit. I see that now I should be able to track my glp1...however I cannot. that would be amzing if I could and I could drop another app I am having to use that helps my dr see progress. I went to add a food and rhe only thing I could put in was the name...it wouldnt let me add any info like cals, or nutrients. I have been tracking for 204 days straight, 50lbs down, all of it should work.

author: Maggi R
text: The new look after the update is awful, I can't tell where anything is and the whole point of the app was to have my meals easy to see and track--now it's just a chore. I'm not renewing my premium since I noticed I've been using it far less since the change due to the extra steps in tracking

author: J M
text: MFP used to be the best calorie tracking app because of how easy it was to use and how it ties into my Garmin watch. Ever since the UI update came along within the past year, I've found using the app to be SUCH a labor. I do not plan on renewing my subscription when the time comes.

author: Stephen Selph
text: Going the wrong direction. New UI is terrible. Go back to how it was! We want to see all foods for each meal without more nested menus and selecting. Perfect for me would be the old format with an option to add a checkbox next to food. I log one day ahead of time and the next day I just eat based on what is logged. would be nice to be able to check off what food has been eaten so far and what hasn't. If the old layout doesn't come back I won't be renewing the premium and I'll be changing apps

author: Saralyn Borg
text: Oh my gosh - the new path forward is horrible. If you need all your macros on a per meal basis? next to impossible. the "old" platform kept things visible and usable, now everything is layered, clunky, and takes so much more time. Who has time for an app that's so expensive, supposed to make things easier and is now more time consuming?! simple things like negative calories for a "meal" (i.e. pregnancy) no longer exist.

author: Annette Scroggs
text: Have used for over 10 years, helping me to lose over 150 lbs - no drugs or surgery. However, the program just gets worse and worse with each update, sometimes fixing one problem but causing 10 other new ones! I'm searching for something else, but so far, nothing I've tried is any better, tho, for me, it's different issues than with MFP. Hanging on here for the time being, but I'm thoroughly exasperated.

author: J B
text: I've been using this app for many years. With the last UI update, there are far more steps than needed to get to a point, my foods have been disappearing, and you can no longer delete multiple things at a time as before. One thing at a time is problematic especially when a reason I now have to do this is its far too easy to pick to use the previous day's meal. It seems apps change things to freshen up but end up ruining the basics and what has worked well. I'd rather have old and functioning.

author: Black Dragon
text: Good but.... there's a major bug with syncing. I connected Health Connect so MFP will automatically sync my workouts from other apps, and it works great, but... the issue is that EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. it syncs it DUPLICATES THE WORKOUTS FROM THE OTHER APP???? So when it says like "Walking, 20 minutes at 01:00 PM" it'll duplicate that entry upwards of 5 times every time you open MFP causing it to sync. And I keep having to delete the duplicates or I have "5000 calories left for the day". Annoying.

author: John Lemons
text: Who is making the decisions for this app? Everything yall do screws things up more and more. Go look at some of the original versions. That is what made yall popular.. from being able to save recipes, to changing calories for the day and it updating correctly to being able to see all of your meals. Also, to find a day I did a certain activity, i have to click a day and scroll all the way down. At least put the Exercise up top with the Calories eaten etc like it use to be.

author: Holly H
text: 6/8/26: I previously rated the app 5 stars. It worked pretty well and was easy to use. The latest update changed the interface, making it hard to use and hard to find the features you're looking for. When viewing the weekly average of Progress, the week dates seem to be hard set and doesn't allow you to change the dates. If I could, I'd roll back to the previous version.

author: Sandy K
text: With the new upgrade you can't slide on the main screen, you'd have to select by date. Can't delete the whole meal, you'd have to do line by line. With premium account you can't set your total calories, it's auto calculated and you can't set your own percentage when it's only set in 5 increments. UPGRADE IS NOT USER FRIENDLY AND NOT WORTH PAYING THE PREMIUM ACCOUNT WHEN THERE'S SO MANY RESTRICTIONS!

author: Cory Boike
text: clunky and gets stuck in a boot-loop sometimes, but otherwise a pretty useful food tracking app that shows macros and calorie requirements, has a decent library of food stuffs as well as the ability to add more and create "meals" as shortcuts for dishes you eat regularly. Overall, a decent app with some flaws that are easily ignored.

author: Wesley
text: MyFitnessPal makes it very easy to track my calories and macros. My only complaint is that there isn't a way to disable the daily streak and pop ups related to it. I don't care how long I've been logging my food because it's automatic for me now. When I have a cheat day and I don't log my food the streak resets so it doesn't matter. And the pop up screen is very annoying. I wish there was a setting to completely disable the streak.

author: Chris Demeur
text: Great for tracking what I've consumed. Terrible at everything else. The dashboard says my calorie goal for the day is 5200...really! No matter, the widget for the same day says my base goal is 1920 for the day. The dashboard says I have nearly 4000 remaining but the widget says under 1200. Doesn't sync exercise or steps from Google Health very well either. I could go on. They want us to pay nearly $100/year for premium?

author: Kip Stamper
text: I like it but I wish adding meals manually, like calories and protein amounts, would allow me to add the recipe name also. It doesn't keep it in the list so you have to go back to the day you entered it and click on it again, if you can remember the date easily. I'm still trying out different aspects and learning but I am really enjoying it. Even if it just keeps me aware to keep track of helps.

author: Brie E
text: This app was perfect and I've gotten good and thorough use out of it! However, the new design is terrible! I liked being able to see everything laid out the way it was before... I shouldn't have to press a ton of buttons to get to see all the food I've eaten in a day. I should be able to quickly glance at my remaining calories and eaten food. I want the old interface back. At least give us a customization option to have the 'classic look.' Until then, one star. Bring it back & Ill change to 5.

author: Renee Hamilton
text: I'm changing my original 5-star rating in 2015 to 3 stars in 2026. Until this week, I loved the app, but now the design is awful. Before, I could see all calorie and food intake in one screen. At the top was the day's calorie allotment, how many I'd eaten, how many I used in exercise and how many I had left. Below that was my food log showing everything I'd eaten, water intake and exercise. Now I have to go to different screens to find the info. The old design was much easier and quicker to use.

author: Jeramie Marquez
text: When I create my own food item, and then I go to create a recipe, there should be a separate menu option of just MY FOODS that I can search through. Instead I have to search through the database and *hope* that I find my food item. And no matter how creative I get with the naming I can never find my own items. MyFitnessPal has been around way too long for something like this to be a problem. It absolutely ruins the experience. 0/10 until y'all figure it out. :)

author: Rebecca Smith
text: The new interface is horrible! Why why why did you make such a drastic change? I can no longer see important stats such as fiber, sodium, etc. Instead they switched to be like every other app on the market and only focus on macros. Forget being able to see what your daily calories are, what has been eaten and what was added in from exercise. If you want that information you have to pull out a calculator. Will be canceling my membership.

author: Oscar Korz
text: I have been using the food diary feature for almost 10 years. I use multiple phones and rarely web, so the diary sync is critical for me. Two months ago (Feb 2026), this stopped working. Changes made in the app no longer save to web or other phones. There is a support thread about it, but it's still broken after two months. This is amateur and totally unacceptable. I can't believe they offer a paid subscription when free features don't even work.

author: Lillie Utley
text: This app is overall good. It would be better if there were other options for entering food, like scanning barcodes or taking a picture without having the premium subscription. Also, recently the weight estimate based on your day's meals and calories has changed. It was once very accurate, but now the estimate is way below a reasonable weight loss amount based on that day's meals and activities. Please correct this!

author: Curt Brackenrich
text: This app is really handy, have yet to scan anything that isn't in the database. Since they were purchased the ads have been a bit more intrusive but it's not too bad. For tracking calories this is the app you want. 2026 UPDATE: I hadn't used the app in years but wow, what a downgrade from before. The app is now cluttered with ads, has a constant push for premium tiers, even basic barcode scanning is now behind a paywall, and their paid tier is by far the priciest out there. No thanks.

author: Thomas Smith
text: I've been using the app for the last 2+ months and have been loving it. BUT today's update has been less than ideal. the UI feels clunkier and less intuitive. The push on the meal planning is a big detractor for me. I may want to check it out, but I don't want to be pushed. I paid a premium so I didn't get the ads. Now on to the positives, the barcode scanner and wealth of preloaded items is fantastic for busy working dad of 3. I can usually jump in and find items quickly.

author: Richard Hoose
text: OMG! With this latest update, the app is practically unusable! Can no longer edit a logged meal. When deleting multiple items, each must be done separately. Far more clicks to log and adjust a meal than ever. I have been a premium user for more than 6 years but I will be looking for a more practical solution than what MFP has become. Avoid this app! UPDATE: I can't believe all the steps now needed to look back at previous meals. WHAT WAS THE DEVELOPER THINKING!?

author: Laurel Hjelsand
text: I've been using MFP for a decade, no issues. The new interface/update is terrible. please change it back or give us the option to use the old interface. It's not user friendly, it isn't logging or saving the food I log, and probably more, I just don't care to find out. None of it makes sense, and is a confusing mess. I'm exhausted after solving problems all day, I don't need more puzzles to solve. I'm deleting, and downloading a different tracking app until MFP reverts back.

author: Derek Knipe
text: DO NOT USE WITH ANDROID!!! This isn't mentioned anywhere, but there is a major flaw that the app doesn't sync if you use with an android based phone. I logged for 8 months with my phone, only to lose 3/4 of my data when they did an update. Apparently, the developers are "aware" of this and working on it and they recommend NOT using the app, but rather the website instead. Completely ridiculous, unprofessional, and a terrible response.

author: Paul Creekmore
text: This app has a few features I need that some others don't, but that advantage is ruined by its poor useability and reliability. Inefficient UI. Lots of garbage in the database. I have to restart the app several times a day when it starts getting slow to respond. The water intake log often forgets entries after initially appearing to accept them. Lately it's been forgetting food entries, too, or placing them on the wrong date. Stops showing my food history in search results. The list goes on.

author: Jordan Scott
text: 4/22 edit: really dislike the new layout, makes logging food much harder. Og: This app could be really good and worth paying for, but currently it's buggy and inconvenient. I can't view or copy from friend's diaries, and it shows my calorie goals instead of theirs when viewing their diary. You can't scroll the ingredient list when it gets too long and runs off the page. You also can't add recipe weights, which is a pain when measuring servings.

author: Holly Daniels
text: The build your own recipe part is hard to use and time consuming. It would be a lot easier to scan bulk ingredients but you can't. Also it only allows about two ingredients then, you cant see what you typing. once you make the recipe and save it, you cant edit it or see what the ingredients are, so later if you forget you can use it, its very poorly made. I love the rest of the app, but I wont renew unless they change that part I will look for one with better ability to build your own recipes.

author: Laquita Johnston
text: This isn't just a calorie counter, it's the way to track & balance an eating plan. When I can see what nutrients I eat, I'm motivated to eat the right foods...not empty calories. I've been using this app for almost 5 months, with great results for my health! 5/26 review: I updated the app & I'm quite disappointed. In the old version, it was easy to see everything at a glance -- logged foods, goal percentages, etc. Now everything is harder to find. Less user friendly. Down from 5 stars to 2.

author: Corinne Henniger
text: Hate the new format. Just changed today. Harder to log and find my stats for the day. May have to find another app for this. Not happy at all. Loved it for years. Not anymore. It's awful. Takes longer to log exercise and meals. Old format was easier. Now I have to turn the screen to see macros, doesn't fit on my screen. This is not progress at all.

author: Hailey Devereaux
text: The app is ok, but hasn't changed a whole lot. Inconsistent foods from people that don't fill in all info is a big problem. It feels overpriced when comparable options are out there. They had some sort of $59.99 offer that I declined when I downloaded and signed into the app but then I thought about it and thought I'd give it a try, but instead when I went to sub it kept pushing my towards the $99 plan. So now I'm giving Garmin Connect+ a try instead.

author: Amy Plank
text: After 20+ years of MFP, I've switched to Cronometer!!! Ooof....what a failure. New update has made the app unusable. Can't enter foods like before, can't scroll to previous days, can't easily add water, etc etc etc. I would never develop something like this for my customers. And good luck using this if you have any visual impairments. I'm going to move on to a different food tracking app. Tired of the push to pay for Premium too.

author: Tom M
text: Why would I ever pay for a premium membership on this app if the free version is this buggy already. Friend requests feature is malfunctioning. It was only after I added them through my phone contacts that it finally worked. Now, the app won't sync with the desktop version for the food diary. Meaning each time I logout of the app, all progress is lost. No use in re-entering data, still won't sync. Support says to use the desktop version for now, completely defeats the purpose of having an app.

author: Justin Murray
text: 2026: App has had major issues for 45+ days. It's listed as a known issue but meanwhile the app isn't saving progress photos since January 30th, and exported CSV data is missing bunch of data points, etc. I would reinstall to see if that fixes it, but their webpage says not to do that until they issue a fix... 2015: Super easy to use. Remembers recipes, eating habits, everything. Have previously lost 60 lbs using it. Back at it to drop some of the weight I put back on since I stopped using it.

author: Madison Henderson
text: This app was great when I used it years ago. Now? It seems functionality is all locked behind a paywall. My chief complaints: 1. the app is super slow and buggy. Entries often don't sync between the app and desktop versions. The recipe import function is so convenient, but editing the imported recipes is such a headache due to the glitches. 2. the food library is wildly inaccurate. one food item from a specific brand will have pages and pages of results, all with different calories.

author: Becky Groseth
text: Despite the fact that scanning disappeared from the free version, I kept the app because I liked the layout better than others. However, the latest update is horrendous. I want to see the entire list of food that I've eaten for a day. I don't want to click on a meal to see it by scrolling through like I used to be able to do. I also liked having the exercise list at the bottom of the food diary. The layout is no longer intuitive. I believe I'll be switching to a different app.

author: Mr. Black
text: So far so good. It lets you search up food items to varying levels of obscurity and track your calorie intake. There are ads and features behind a paywall, but if you're just looking for a calorie watcher with an extensive database of food items this is a good free app for that. Update: -1 star. App is randomly logging me out now and also the changes to the UI are bad.

author: Kayla Thompson
text: update: the new update is absolutely trash and it's worse now than it ever was. I love the concept of this app. I've used it for years. I had the free premium trial because I did enjoy the barcode scanner... but now almost everything I've scanned has had incorrect information. Why pay for something that doesn't work even half the time? I will continue using the free app for now, but I can't justify the premium price for the barcode scanner if all the nutritional info rarely matches.

author: jocindy marsh
text: OMG, the new update app is so irritating! Changed my raiting because they took away the barcode scan option I've used free for years and added it to the premium pay option. Looks like a greedy move to me. Obviously they weren't getting enough people to purchase the premium option as it was, so they take away what was the most used feature (that was free) and move it to paid only option. Extremely disappointed in My Fitness Pal! I think it might be time to find another food logging app.

author: Meghin
text: New UI complicates adding foods, reverts back to same nutrient overview even when I change it. I need easy access to my full diary because I plan meals in advance and check to see what I'm eating. Once I get my recipes off here I'll delete the app. they responded to my review. I can use the app, it just sucks and takes a bunch of extra time for something I used to do at a glance. it's no longer functional for my needs. I meal plan on my own: I don't need AI for that.

author: Esther Cotton
text: 2026 - They've somehow managed to make things even worse and more unaccessible. 2 stars. --- 2019 - Been using it for years, but my love for it has declined (from 5 stars to 3) due to numerous server issues and syncing issues MyFitnessPal keeps having. It's especially frustrating for a paying customer (no longer), because my money is wasted if I'm unable to use the app.

author: bhanson1994
text: After 7+ years, I've finally had the last straw and need to move to a different app. I wanted to give a detailed laundry list to maybe help with constructive feedback, but I was limited by characters, so basically, it was making it difficult to get to the section that was actually useful, intrusive ads, more intrusive ads, an misguided update, but the final straw was having several months of data erased out of nowhere. So goodbye, and hopefully a new paradigm will get me on track.

author: Tara Grant
text: This used to be a wonderful app. I cannot get this app to read Health Connect for accurate exercise or steps. The log for food is okay. and I like being able to input the recipes for calorie counting. I paid the subscription. what a waste of money. As of 03/22/2026, this is still a major issue No matter how.many times I sync, it stops recording steps.

author: S M
text: Uninstalled. Not sure why, but today the layout changed and it's terrible. I didn't update the app, nor do I have it set to download automatically. Before, I could view every item in breakfast, lunch and dinner on one page. Now, multiple items are grouped together and I have to do an extra step to go into each section to view all the items, including water/exercise. It's discombobluated. Can we PLEASE have the option to change it back? What was the point of messing with a perfectly good thing?

author: Barbara A
text: I have used this app for years but the new update that occurred mid April 2026 is terrible to the point where I'm deleting it. It's not "oh it's new and I have to get used to it." No, they've made substantial changes that make it so unfriendly to use. I am now clicking more & more just to add my food & water intake. They use grey font on black background, it's hard to see your net calories total due to this. They separated breakfast, lunch, etc- you don't have access to all the info on one page.

author: Frank Lee
text: I haven't had the app but a few days, but so far I am really liking it. To be continued..... Well... had to make an adjustment here after less than a week with the app. The app started adding double the steps I actually take a day, which doubles burnt calories and calorie deficit. spent way too long trying to figure out how to fix the problem. Done everything that was suggested, and it's still doing it. Not paying for an app that can't accurately log correct, and such important information.

author: Miranda Ray
text: I've used this app almost daily for 11 yrs. It has been very useful for me. Which means I spend a lot of time entering things. This new update is awful I wish I could take back the update. I spent more time trying to figure out where & how to enter stuff than I care to admit. I liked seeing all my food for the day & "add" right all on the same page & nutrition icon. Now you have to hit "view all" or "log" (which is very small) & More.Why? So I spend more time on the app? Sorry I might jump ship.

author: Luke Hancox
text: for over a month the app and web version no longer sync. the problem is that all apps that use MFP data (like fitbit) pull from the web data. so now you have to enter everything on the web version which is a horrible UI and just not convenient. this is not a small temporary hiccup. it's been over a month!! their response? "we're working on it." they promise the next update will fix it. it doesn't. radio silence again.

author: Ryan Christensen
text: I've been using this for several years on and off. in the last year I used it extensively to lose 90 pounds and achieve my goal weight, along with major health improvements. But what deranged lunatic came up with the recent update (3/3/2025)? This went from being intuitive and easy to use, to literally hiding the information you want behind to see. I can't see what I've logged without several clicks and the app fighting against me seeing my log. Stupid, and I'm probably deleting it! (4/23/26)

author: April Bagnall
text: I use the premium version so I have access to all nutrition information. I love the fasting timer. Really helps to keep consistent. Con: I can no longer sync my steps from my samsung watch. It is frustrating but, I did create a work rough work around. It's probably not accurate but I do what I can. edit- and now I am deleting this app. I can't get logged in and this not the first, second, or third time.

author: Deanne
text: They updated the app and now there is no way to delete food you entered in in error. Update: 04/25 I have tap everywhere on the app and under "today" brings up a calender. The today at the buttom just brings you back home. I do not see a way to delete food. The "log yesterday" is right under the the log button and you can easily hit it and enter the wrong food. I personally do not like this layout change.

author: Lori P
text: Don't like this new look, everything is more difficult to see & enter with more touches to do it, can't delete an entire meal only one item at a time. The meal calorie numbers are very small & faint on the main screen. Please bring back the diary where you can see your whole day's food on one screen. It might be time to find a new app to use....

author: Cady
text: I hate the new updated look. It moved where the diary was so now it is harder to find and edit what foods are in there. You are also now not able to see the exact amount of calories you have burned from exercise. They also took away the button to finish the diary entry and it told you what your weight could be if you ate the same way for five weeks. Essentially they took away the diary and just turned it into the nutrition tab.

author: Nic Kibler (Aphemra)
text: The app does as advertised but I won't give it more than 1 star until they fix the sync issue. New phone season is here and everyone who is upgrading will be stuck losing any unsynced data or, like me, be forced to use my old device to track calories until they fix the problem. It has been an issue for months now and it's honestly unacceptable. I'll be finding an alternative app if it isn't corrected soon.

author: J P
text: hey there's a new bug that's annoying me to the point of avoiding the app. when I type something in like "chicken", the app automatically searches after I type "chi" and then refreshes the app and puts the cursor at the front of the word I just typed, so I end up typing "ckenchi" and I get an error because that's not a food item. It's extremely annoying.

author: Heather Sanchez
text: previous versions were better. they updated the food log and made it so there are more buttons to click and screens to go through to get to where you wanted. instead of being able to add food from the first screen you have to click to 2-3 screens later. the food suggestions tries to be smarter, but is worse. it's supposed to filter by recent or most used and foods that i used 2 days prior don't show up as an option.

author: Kylee Morris
text: Not loving the new update. Its not convenient to have to go to the top to change days and then have to open each meal separately and repeat. I plan multiple days ahead and need to be able to quickly and easily see my foods. I wish they would add the swipping feature back to see the different days, and not have only 1 food per meal show on the main page.

author: Emily Christenson
text: Been using this app for 5 yrs and this update is terrible! The layout and interface is completely different and not for the better. I have ADHD so I need to plan my meals the day before and then eat based off that, otherwise I snack too much or don't eat at all. The condensed look on the home screen makes that much more difficult. Now I have to click on each meal to see what it contains, rather than just scroll up and down to remind myself of what I need to eat in the day. Trash. Please undo.

author: Lizzy
text: I've been using this app almost daily for 10 years, but this new app update has ruined this app. I'm now actively searching for a replacement. I can't see all my meals at once, creating a problem of items being missed or logged incorrectly. The macros at the top is nice, but if I can't see if my meals are logged correctly or how many calories I have left, it's useless. Why change the front interface screen to make it HARDER to log meals? I've never seen so much joint outrage for something.

author: Tad Thompson
text: I can't imagine the person who green-lit this update uses the app, because absolutely ruined its functionality. Figuring out what I've logged is profoundly cumbersome now that it requires a separate click to see each meal. I routinely have 10+ entries in a meal, and the inability to alter their order of appearance makes it more difficult to confirm I've entered everything correctly and haven't double-counted. Glad I found a way to revert to an older version, because the new one is garbage.

author: Michael Goodson
text: Current release seems to have messed up a huge amount of my previous logging. I just saw on their website that the Android app isn't syncing with the website, but the app doesn't give you a warning. a lot of my previously logged meals now have recipes that clearly have calorie values but are entering zeros as those values. Online, it looks like much of my previously logged data has duplicate entries for every item. I don't know what happened and if they can fix this.

author: Kyle Snide
text: This app used to be the best app for weight loss, gain, just tracking your nutrition goals in general for anyone. This app truly helped me achieve my goals and I lost 20+ lbs and looked and felt the best I ever had. Took a break from tracking then came back and noticed you had to pay to scan barcodes! Decided to go to calAI. Once my year sub ended, came back to MFP, and it's even worse. Can't even track macros correctly. Now the new layout is awful. This app fell apart. It was perfect. No more

author: Nepsi Cola
text: This new update has seriously messed with something backend for the data base connection. I cannot log any foods without creating a new one or having to sign out and log back into the app. Please fix, it is extremely frustrating to have a majority of the app just not work correctly. (Edit) No, it was not a meal logging issue. it seemed to be an app issue along with, why cant I delete meals???? Like. I have a bunch I either messed up portions or just dont use anymore but they now just sit there.

author: Amber Shockley
text: The new update brought me to review the app with a one-star rating. I see others feel the same way. Please, please, please go back to the old design. I liked the circle that showed how much exercise impacted my "calories left" for the day. I liked that calories consumed, calories burned, and calories left were all at the top and easy to see. The app doesn't seem to be syncing with GoogleFit anymore - I'm used to a lag, but now it's not registering or converting them to calories burned.

author: Maria Estrada
text: This app really helps log your food and exercise. Totally recommended! Update 5.22.26 This app isn't as good as it used to be. Even with the premium version, the barcode never worked and they changed the style completely. The worst part was when I used to be able to copy a meal, but now I have to insert it individually. It's kind of frustrating. I can't even find the recipes I logged when I first started. Also, it doesn't connect with my Google Pixel watch.

author: M B
text: Edit #2: CANCELLED. Edit: I would like a refund for remainder of the actual app I paid for. This app is now unusable with the most recent update because one can no longer see a complete day (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks) as a simple list, with each of those meals listing protein, carbs, etc Not every app needs to have "card views" that require endless scrolling and actually show less information than before. Now I am out 5 months of Premium that I paid for and have basically been ripped off.

author: Kasey Richardson
text: New interface they've forced onto the user is terrible. It's not intuitive at all and it makes what was once a fairly streamlined logging process a frustratingly tedious slog. I've used MFP for years and it seems to get worse with each major update. If you're at all serious about tracking your food/calories/macros don't waste your time with this app.

author: Lydia L
text: I originally lost and maintened a loss of 50+ lbs with MFP. Now that I've gone through pregnancy, I need to do the same thing again, but this app feels completely unusable. I can't easily set my calorie goal. I get no say in how much I want to restrict myself. Everything is about the paid subscription. I'm choosing something else, and will be recommending against this app.

author: James Megna
text: Edit: I am deducting one star for the canned response from MFP. The app now receives a one star rating. The April changes to the UI are bad. I don't want to see macros. They are forced visible. I always fail the macros on low carb but I eat 1500 calories a day and I'm doing alright. Data entry per meal is more cumbersome. Seeing one day of diet information is not the default. Everything seems to take more clicks to accomplish. Everything else everyone else mentioned.

author: Grace McCarter
text: has become useless over the day. I usually log w/PC because it's easier, &then I check in on things via the app. It's always been buggy and I have to tell it "complete day" and then it populates. The new update apparently needs you to log something from in the app(annoying but whatevs) but now it doesn't even sync! I chose this because I know it's also popular in Japan and I hope to move there someday but time to break my 450+ day streak & go to loseit, I guess. I had the whole week planned.🫠

author: Brittany Jones
text: I've used this app for years and it has been very helpful in keeping me on track with macros. Recently though I've noticed, when I log my food it does not calculate the macros accurately. Like for example the food I logged added up to 70g in protein but the app told me there was 105g of protein. So I'm sad I haven't been actually meeting my protein goals because the app was telling me I was...if you guys could fix this, I would appreciate it, because I do love this app otherwise!!

author: Brenda P.
text: Update 4/23/26 new update makes it where the diary only shows one food you logged and says "and 4 more." No!!! I want to still see my FULL diary when I look at it. Update I'm dropping my 5 stars down to 3 for now. I've used this app for years. Just recently the search function doesn't search my existing foods and give me a matching list. I have to do a full search and choose a result to use each time.

author: Terah G
text: As of the most recent update at the beginning of May, the app no longer tracks my steps through any of the options I have available (Google Fit, Samsung Health, or Android Health Connect). I've tried disconnecting and reconnecting them all, separately, multiple times. Including clearing the caches. This is incredibly frustrating as now MFP doesn't allow me to properly track my calories, and does not allow any manual input of step counts. Please fix this, or allow us to input steps manually.

author: Kristen Darling
text: MFP changed their user interface completely. It used to be user friendly and now it's so hard to track anything, find out what you ate, and hard to track your micronutrients like fiber. Check reddit and MFP threads. Don't get it until you know it's been fixed. Certainly don't upgrade to Premium hoping it will be better. That was helpful at first but now they've added so much extra stuff to make it "fancier" but it's absolute garbage now. I will be looking for another app and cancelling premium.

author: Linda Ward
text: I left a 5 star review in 2013. After using this app for over 13 years, the new update (and character limit) have forced me to replace it with a one star review. The new UI is beyond terrible. The diary used to be simple to use; now it's a nightmare. And the number of calories left for the day? No longer big bold numbers; now it's tiny numbers you have to scroll to find. Other reviews show I'm far from alone in my dislike of the changes. Way to get rid of your (formerly) faithful users.

author: M Mishka
text: Absolutely HATE the new update. I refuse to keep using it. the layout is not user friendly whatsoever and is not "simplified". there was absolutely no need to change the layout, but apparently they just wanted to completely destroy the app. my biggest grievance- it automatically is adding my exercise into my calories without showing that it added it to my calories.Im trying to LOSE weight, I am working out to be in a larger deficit not to eat more. RIP MFP

author: Mary All
text: I found the new update has taken an app that was easy to use for logging my meals and made it far more difficult. I often wait to log my last meal until the next day and I'm finding it more difficult and confusing to do that now. I understand there is always a learning curve when changes happen but it's been awhile and am still finding myself feeling frustrated after the update.
